ops.title: Releasing the cc-transcript family — cc-pushback→cc-steer rename; parallel sessions grab version tags (ship the leftover migration as the next patch); live-fleet shared-working-copy clobbering → quiescence polls + tight windows + path-scoped jj commi

ops.body:
Release-process facts for the cc-transcript family (cc-transcript, captain-hook, cc-steer, cc-sentiment, cc-context/bench), from the v8 rollout (2026-07-03) and the migrate-to-latest round (2026-07-05). **cc-pushback was renamed to cc-steer** (repo `github.com/yasyf/cc-steer`, PyPI `cc-steer`); `~/Code/cc-pushback` is now a `MOVED.md` tombstone and its old `cc-pushback-migrate` worktree's gitdir moved with it (breaks `git worktree remove` → `rm -rf` + `git -C cc-steer worktree prune`). For the `[tool.uv] environments` macOS/Linux lock scoping (required in every consumer), see [[cc-transcript-v8-downstream-uv-lock]].

**ALWAYS diagnose against `origin/main`, never the local checkout.** In these jj-colocated repos the local working copy sits at a *stale detached HEAD* (jj hasn't synced it), so `git log`/`git grep`/`git describe HEAD` on the local tree routinely show pre-migration code and mismatched tags — this caused false "regression"/"orphaned release/lost work" alarms **twice** (captain-hook, then cc-sentiment: `git describe HEAD`=`v0.2.128-1` while `origin/main` was already at `v0.2.129`=the published migration). Before ever concluding work was lost or a release is orphaned, check `git rev-parse origin/main` and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag> origin/main`. Also expect the local main checkout to hold an *unpushed parallel-session feature commit* diverged from `origin/main` at the last release (e.g. captain-hook local `383cef4c` steering pack 0.4.0 vs my pushed fixes on `origin/main`) — leave it, it rebases; a FF-only push (`<sha>:refs/heads/main`) can't clobber it. Recover genuinely-unmerged fix branches (verify with `git cherry origin/main <branch>`: `+`=unique/unmerged, `-`=already landed) by cherry-picking the *fix commit itself* onto current `origin/main` (the branch's own base may be ancient/pre-v8 — ignore the huge `diff origin/main..branch`, `git show <sha>` is the real change).

**Migration branches drift under parallel work.** The family repos are jj-colocated (detached HEAD; use git only — the user actively pushes to them mid-release). Migration branches get cut, then main advances: during v8, captain-hook's `cc-transcript-v8` branch ended up +6/−37 vs main (main had cut 2 releases meanwhile); cc-sentiment's was only 2 behind. Redo = REBASE the preserved branch onto current main, don't redo from scratch — the work survives on `refs/heads/*` + `refs/jj/keep/*` (verify with `git for-each-ref --contains <sha>`). mergiraf auto-resolves most conflicts; a v8 export-list conflict (feature added exports, migration removed top-level `Command`→`types.Command`) resolves as feature-additions ∪ migration-removal. Rebase onto the LATEST main right before pushing — it keeps moving; push `HEAD:main` with an `is-ancestor` fast-forward guard.

**Freshly-published versions lag on the uv index CDN.** Right after a `v*` tag publishes and the wheel is confirmed on the PyPI JSON API, `uv lock` in a downstream repo may still see only the PRIOR version ("only capt-hook<=6.5.0 available … unsatisfiable"). It's a Fastly CDN propagation lag on the simple-index edge uv reads (~6 min for capt-hook 7.0.0). `--refresh-package <name>` busts it once propagated; a fresh `uv cache clean <name>` helps; avoid bare `uv lock --refresh` (re-fetches everything, times out). So sequence family releases with a gap and re-lock downstreams last.

**ccxbench (cc-context/bench) test harness:** `uv run pytest` fails with "No module named spawnllm" because pytest isn't a declared dep, so uv runs it OUTSIDE the project env. Use `uv run --with pytest python -m pytest`. cc-context itself is a Go/Homebrew package (`ccx`); `bench` is an internal Python benchmark with no PyPI release — wave-2 there is just dep-bump + re-lock + push to main.

**GitHub Pages deploy flakes:** cc-transcript + captain-hook both hit `publish-docs → Deploy to GitHub Pages: "Deployment failed, try again later" (error_count: 10)` while `build-docs` stayed green — a transient GitHub-side infra issue, re-runnable, NOT a docs-build problem and NOT release-blocking (PyPI release is a separate workflow). Related: [[docs-build-sidebar-cost]], [[cc-transcript-build-env]].

**Migrate-to-latest round (2026-07-05) — additional mechanics:**
- **Parallel sessions release version tags out from under you.** captain-hook `v8.4.0` and cc-steer `v0.9.0` were both tagged+published by other sessions from current `origin/main` — each shipped a feature but WITHOUT the pending dep-floor migration, so the migration ships as the next **patch** (v8.4.1, v0.9.1) on top (the tag points at the pre-migration commit; your migration commit is still a clean FF child of it). Guard every release with `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` (FF) **and** `git ls-remote --tags origin v<X>` (collision) *immediately* before tag+push; both fired this run and stopped a clobber. Tag-driven repos: `release-pypi.yml` on `push: tags:["v*"]`. cc-sentiment auto-releases on `push: branches:[main]` (version-strategy `auto-tag`, base `0.2` → mints `0.2.130`) — the main push IS the release trigger, no hand tag.
- **`uv lock --upgrade-package <name>`, NOT `--refresh-package`, picks up a fresh publish that still satisfies the range.** bench's `capt-hook>=8,<9` already locked 8.4.0, so `uv lock` kept 8.4.0 (still valid) and `--refresh-package` only refreshes cached metadata — it won't upgrade a valid pin. `uv lock --upgrade-package capt-hook` pulled 8.4.1. (Distinct from the CDN-lag `--refresh-package` case above, which is about the version not being visible at all yet.)
- **Test deps in a `[project.optional-dependencies] dev` EXTRA break a naive gate.** cc-steer & spawnllm keep pytest under a `dev` extra, which `uv sync --locked` does NOT install; `uv run --no-sync pytest` then falls through PATH to a foreign venv (e.g. sibling `cc-transcript/.venv`) → phantom `ModuleNotFoundError`. Mirror the repo's own `ci.yml`: `uv sync --extra dev --locked` + `uv run pytest`. Always run gates with `--python 3.13` — uv defaults to CPython 3.14 and spacy 3.8.x ships cp313-only wheels, so a 3.14 install fails spuriously.
- **great-docs git-pins retire to `great-docs>=0.14`.** captain-hook (`@d8540ae2`) and spawnllm (`@main`) tracked great-docs main for the GitHub-widget stats; those ship in published **0.14.1**, so flip to `>=0.14` (docs build stays green, "widget injected" confirmed). cc-steer additionally had `great-docs>=0.13,<0.14` *conflicting* with its own `cc-transcript>=8.1` (which needs >=0.14) — the migration cleared it.
- **ccxbench `.fixtures` corpus:** 2 `TestLargeContextBuilder` tests in `bench/tests/test_harness.py` read `cfg.fixtures_root/{click,gorilla-mux}` — a **gitignored** corpus of cloned repos absent in a fresh worktree → `FileNotFoundError`. **No cc-context CI job runs the bench suite at all**, so it's neither release-blocking nor a regression; a floor-bump push leaves 62 pass / 2 corpus-fail / 1 skip. (Confirms/extends the `uv run --with pytest` note above.)

**Follow-ups round (2026-07-11) — live-fleet concurrency mechanics:**
- **Concurrent sessions clobber uncommitted work in shared jj working copies.** Multiple live sessions write to the same checkouts (cc-transcript, captain-hook, cc-context simultaneously that day). A `jj` op from the other session (snapshot/commit) silently reverts or sweeps your uncommitted edits — a fully-verified rustfmt pass and a proven-green captain-hook migration were both wiped mid-verification. Working pattern: (1) poll quiescence first (`jj op log --limit 1` timestamp + `jj st` dirtiness; ~30 min op-silence is a safe window, ~5 min is not); (2) keep the uncommitted window tight — apply deterministic/pre-verified changes and commit IMMEDIATELY, run the long verification AFTER the commit, fix forward with amend/second commit (safe while unpushed); (3) in a dirty foreign tree, use a **path-scoped** `jj commit <paths> -m ...` naming exactly your files — it leaves the foreign session's modified-uncommitted files in `@` untouched (verified: captain-hook landing left 7 foreign files intact); post-commit fixes must also be path-scoped (bare `jj squash` would sweep foreign files); (4) re-check `jj op log` immediately before the commit and abort if a foreign op appeared; (5) agents in shared checkouts get an explicit stop-condition: "if `jj st` shows files that aren't yours, STOP — don't commit".
- **Version numbers race too:** the v10.7.0→followups session found v10.8.0 AND v11.0.0 shipped by parallel sessions within hours; a planned breaking release renumbers (v11→v12) rather than fighting for the tag.
